newsitem.title: USA: Meredith dilution from First Media deal cut.
newsitem.headline: Meredith dilution from First Media deal cut.

text.p: Meredith Corp said Monday it expected less dilution to earnings per share from the previously announced acquisition of several television stations from First Media Television.

Meredith said dilution from the First Media deal is now expected to be between $0.08 and $0.10 a share in the first year and about half that amount in the second year. The deal is expected to be accretive by year three.
Originally, Meredith said, the First Media deal was expected to cut earnings by $0.15 to $0.17 a share in fiscal 1998 and half that in fiscal 1999.

Dilution was lessened by the agreement, announced today, for Meredith to acquire WFSB-TV, the CBS affiliate serving Hartford-New Haven, Conn., in exchange for WCPX-TV, the CBS affiliate serving Orlando, Fla.
WCPX is one of the stations that Meredith agreed to purchase from First Media.
The deal to acquire WFSB from Post-Newsweek Stations Inc, a subsidiary of Washington Post Co, called for an exchange of assets plus a $60 million cash payment to Meredith.
